chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Abdul Kareem, from al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And for the divorced women a provision with goodness; this is a right upon the pious.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her provision, after her waiting period ends, is upon the affluent according to his ability, and upon the poor according to his ability.'
And how can he not provide for her while she is in her waiting period, hoping for him and he for her; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings about between them whatever He wills.
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the man is affluent, he provides for his wife with a slave boy and a slave girl; and the poor provides with wheat, barley, raisins, clothing, and dirhams.'
And indeed, Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) provided for a wife of his with a slave girl, and he did not divorce any woman except that he provided for her.

key_terms.مَتَاعٌ: Provision given to a divorced woman

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and method of providing for a divorced woman according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the Quranic command of 'muta'' (gift of provision) for divorced women, specifying that it is paid after the 'iddah' concludes and is scaled according to the husband's financial capacity. It highlights the practical application of this ruling by noting that provision can take diverse forms—ranging from slaves and food to clothing and coins—and cites Imam Hasan (peace be upon him) as a precedent for ensuring every divorced wife receives such provision. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the husband's duty to provide a final gift as a mark of respect and closure, distinct from the maintenance during the waiting period.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr Al Bazanty, from Abdul Kareem, from Al Halby,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:241] And for the divorced women a provision with the goodness; this is a right upon the pious.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He provides for her after the fulfillment of her waiting period upon the financial solvent in accordance to his ability, and upon the poor according to his ability.

And how can he not provide for her and she is in her waiting period, she is hoping for him and he is hoping for her; and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would bring about whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the man was affluent upon him is the provision for his wife with the slave and the maid, and the poor should provide with the wheat, and the barley, and the raisins, and the clothes, and the Dirhams;

and Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> provided for a wife of his<sup>asws</sup> with a maid, and he<sup>asws</sup> did not divorce his<sup>asws</sup> woman except that he<sup>asws</sup> provided for her’.
en.sarwar: Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and a number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Bazantiy who has said the following: “Certain persons of our people have mentioned that benefiting a divorced woman is obligatory.’”
